findings.text: In a context WITHOUT the Promise intrinsic, merely creating an async function or async generator object leaks a GC object; QuickJS then fails assert(list_empty(&rt->gc_obj_list)) in JS_FreeRuntime and the PROCESS ABORTS (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN in the debug build). Bisected with 7+4 probes (probe commits 409e19e, 1d886fc). Mitigation: Promise intrinsic added (probe shows no leak), global Promise deleted, jobs never executed. Consequence: an in-process native engine can take down the host on hostile source; the worker-process lane is MANDATORY before production use, not optional hardening.

Scripts that never reach an engine poll (about every 10,000 branch/call steps) cost 0 provider units; long C builtins and parsing are not interruptible in-process. Matches EXPR-PROVIDER-04: needs worker deadline.
QuickJS out-of-memory is a catchable InternalError; heap stays bounded by the limit but script can swallow the error and continue.

Without JS_AddIntrinsicEval even the embedder cannot compile source (JS_EvalInternal throws), so no trusted-compile-realm split is possible through the safe wrapper; only the name/constructor hardening above is available. Completeness of denial is NOT_PROVEN.

decisions.text: rquickjs Function::new requires 'js-lifetime closures, so a borrowed &mut HostBridge cannot be captured; avoided unsafe lifetime erasure with deterministic miss/replay (crate keeps forbid(unsafe_code)).
ScriptedEngine interprets fixed command words only and must never grow into a JS evaluator.
MOT-259 has no runtime-error code: thrown reference error -> ReferenceMissing, other thrown -> Unsupported (UNVERIFIED mapping).
motion-js-es2018@1 is a working identifier, not from the spec.
Wall-clock deadline is a cooperative resource guard; the deterministic budget is Fuel. Both surface as Budget; kind only visible in ProviderStats denial counters.
A Budget error returned by HostRead is mapped to BudgetKind::Fuel and cannot be caught by script code.
